originality.rationale: The novelty claimed is the fully sharp finite-budget risk/schedule theorem, nonzero residual at the optimum, and the exact constant-step reconstruction-monotonicity frontier, not the already known failure of plain randomized Gauss–Seidel to find the minimum-norm solution. The 2024 source establishes the algorithm and weak/conditional stronger convergence; the 2015 source proves the qualitative underdetermined failure but not this finite-budget optimal design. Targeted mathematical-record searches and the 52 accessible own scientific claims revealed no implication of the complete result. Equivalent formulations in older stochastic-approximation weight-optimality literature are a residual risk.
residual_risks: A finite-horizon equal-weight schedule with this risk may appear in older randomized approximation or optimal stochastic-approximation literature under different terminology.
The motivating operator is a very narrow but canonical rank-deficient inverse problem; no extension to general tomography or arbitrary operators is asserted.

value.rationale: An exact natural small inverse-problem model shows residual minimization and minimum-norm reconstruction are different finite-budget objectives. The theorem uniquely optimizes all deterministic step schedules, identifies why deliberately leaving a residual minimizes expected error, and determines the exact threshold where constant steps improve measured residual while worsening reconstruction. The schedule is implementable with only coordinate updates and remains at or below 1/b, a practically relevant conservative step scale.
